documentSummary.purpose: Provide the authoritative human-readable Project definition and current interpretation for Inventory Management while keeping intrinsic identity, Resource routing, relationships, implementation truth, and execution evidence with their own authorities.

documentSummary.summary: Inventory Management is a Klinswork Project concerned with reliable knowledge and operational control of inventory. Its principal known System is Inventory 3.0. The Project is defined independently of its current name, hierarchy, repository location, application, datastore, Resource set, deployment, or operational environment. The current exemplar now includes a Project Identity record, local README, human-readable Project Summary, and this structured companion sidecar; System-local documentation, discovery testing, Viewer testing, Resource reconciliation, and final reusable Project Definition extraction remain.
documentSummary.confidence: high for documented Project-definition facts; current implementation state remains only partially reverified

keyPoints.title: Inventory Management is the Project
keyPoints.description: Inventory Management is the durable Project identity; Inventory 3.0 is the principal known System, not a synonym for the Project.

keyPoints.title: Project ID remains unassigned
keyPoints.description: The permanent PROJ-### value is intentionally blank until formal allocation; names, folders, relationships, and historical numbering must not be used to invent one.

keyPoints.title: Operational function is inventory-state control
keyPoints.description: The Project covers identification, state establishment, controlled state change, event history, verification, and operational use of inventory information.

keyPoints.title: Boundaries are functional
keyPoints.description: Scheduling, Task Assignment and Tracking, Documentation, Meadows Housekeeping, and Inventory 3.0 remain distinct even when they are related to Inventory Management.

keyPoints.title: Resource identity is separate from Project identity
keyPoints.description: Applications, workbooks, scripts, datasets, deployments, SDS records, and documentation artifacts are Resources or related artifacts whose current routing belongs in the Resource Registry.

keyPoints.title: Current implementation claims remain bounded
keyPoints.description: The Project Summary does not claim current deployment behavior, live quantities, schemas, or successful tests without current implementation and execution evidence.

keyPoints.title: Project Definition exemplar is now layered
keyPoints.description: The exemplar now separates identity, orientation, narrative Project definition, and machine-readable summary interpretation into different records with different authority roles.

keyPoints.title: Historical terminology is preserved
keyPoints.description: Earlier records may use application-centered or System-centered terminology and should remain as evidence rather than being silently rewritten.

keyPoints.title: Resume work progressively
keyPoints.description: Future sessions should load Project Identity, README, Project Summary, relevant System context, Registry-resolved Resources, workflow state, Activities, and deeper history only as needed.

keyPoints.title: Next layer is Inventory 3.0 documentation
keyPoints.description: The next concrete work is the Inventory 3.0 README, System Summary, and companion sidecar, followed by manifest and Viewer verification.

general.summary: Inventory Management is the durable Klinswork Project for reliable inventory knowledge and control. Inventory 3.0 is its principal known System. The Project definition now separates intrinsic identity, orientation, narrative interpretation, and machine-readable metadata.
keyPoints: Project identity is independent of implementation and location.
Permanent Project and System IDs remain intentionally unassigned.
Resources and relationships retain separate authorities.
The next work is System documentation and Viewer/discovery testing.

technical.summary: This sidecar structures the Inventory Management Project Summary using the generic-document 3.0-draft sidecar schema. It preserves the Markdown source as narrative authority and references project-identity.json separately as the Project Identity Entity Record.
keyPoints: Entity Record discovery remains a pending Viewer concern

projectSpecificLessons: A Project Definition works better as coordinated records with distinct authorities than as one oversized record.
Inventory Management can be defined durably without assigning a premature PROJ-### value.
Inventory 3.0 can be described as the principal System without making System identity intrinsic Project identity.
generalLessons: Entity Records and document sidecars require different authority semantics.
Repository locality helps navigation but should not define semantic identity.
Machine-readable companions should preserve, not replace, human-readable narrative authority.

recurringProblems.pattern: Historical documentation often organizes around the most visible implementation artifact.
